newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices plunge, except for Shenzhen B.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices plunge, except for Shenzhen B.

text.p: China's stock markets plunged on Tuesday, except Shenzhen's hard currency B share index, which rose on buying of Chongqing Chang'an Automobile Co.
Shanghai's foreign currency B shares fell about 1.9 percent on Tuesday as investors continued to sell shares of property developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development Co, brokers said.
The B index fell 1.410 points, or 1.94 percent, to 71.300 points on moderate turnover of $6.212 million, compared with $10.067 million on Monday.
"The fall in Lujiazui affected sentiment," an analyst at a Japanese securities firm in Shanghai said. "Lujiazui reported poor results because the Shanghai property market isn't very good."
Lujiazui fell $0.118, or 9.93 percent, to $1.070, becoming Tuesday's biggest B share loser.
The company on Friday posted net profits of 179.376 million yuan for the first half of 1997, down 67 percent from the first half of 1996, sparking a sell-off that began on Monday.
Of 47 B shares, 44 shares traded on Tuesday with 27 down, 14 up and three flat.
Recently listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal Co was the most actively traded B share on profit-taking. It fell $0.020, or 4.37 percent, to $0.438 on volume of about 1.4 million shares.
Shanghai's domestic currency A shares tumbled on talk some companies would soon announce poor interim results, which caused heavy selling in the afternoon session, brokers said.
The A index plunged 39.413 points, or 3.18 percent, to 1,200.153 points on turnover of 3.820 billion yuan against 4.846 billion on Monday.
Shanghai's SSE30 blue-chip index plummeted 146.277 points, or 3.92 percent, to 3,589.552 points.
Shenzhen's hard currency B share index edged up slightly at the close on Tuesday, with a late afternoon burst of buying of Chongqing Chang'an Automobile Co Ltd, brokers said.
The B index rose 0.36 points, or 0.27 percent, to 133.25 on turnover of HK$59 million, against Monday's HK$44 million.
"A last-hour Chang'an buying frenzy drove the B index up," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.
The car maker's shares closed at their 10 percent limit-up level of HK$3.80 after reporting on Monday a 41 percent year-on-year rise in its first-half net profits.

Strong buying in Fiyta Holdings Ltd, which on Tuesday reported an 85 percent jump year-on-year in first-half net profits, also lifted the B index. The stock closed at its 10 percent limit-up level of 6.16 yuan.
Shenzhen's domestic currency A share market, however, plunged 14.78 points, or 3.74 percent, to 380.41 on thin turnover of 4.2 billion yuan compared with 5.4 billion yuan on Monday.
Some analysts said the A index was weighed down by the relatively high P/E ratio, which they said averaged around 20 times.
Among the A shares, the biggest loser was Changzheng Machine Tool Co Ltd, which plunged to its 10 percent limit-down level of 5.30 yuan.
